MX17 at LNL · target designs in Geant4 · 27 Oct 2026

Build the 45° diamond window, not the Cu hemisphere: the copper shell costs ×9 in days. DREAM and the scintillators cope if the single-arm trigger is prescaled; watch the window’s Mo x-rays in the Micromegas and fluorine at 1.10 MeV.

Geant4 run L10: both designs with the photographed beam line, the arms as built and with the big plastics, X17, M1/E1 IPC (γ₀ and γ₁), EPC, and γ-line libraries for the singles. Nuclear yields from measured data.

3

Details

Every lepton crosses the Cu shell; near 90° from the apex it runs nearly tangent (~30 % X₀), and the shell converts the ⁸Be γ: EPC is 46 % of the background against 5 % for the window. 0° costs ×1.35 against 45° (rings and end piece in the 90° plane). 1.03 MeV costs +15–18 % (more direct capture). As-built numbers are statistics-limited (±30–50 %).

The window itself is better than the flat design; its Ø20 Al end piece costs the 3 degrees

Leptons at 90–140° cross the Ø20 tube wall at grazing incidence. Mount the window on a wide, short adapter (open to ≥ Ø60 within a few mm): nothing within ~12 mm behind the window plane at r = 10 mm.

No beam neutrons: ⁷Li(p,n) opens at 1.881 MeV, ⁶⁵Cu(p,n) at 2.17, ¹³C(p,n) at 3.2. Cu/Mo (p,γ) and Coulomb excitation < 10⁻¹⁰ per proton.

5

Details

Yields: ⁸Be from Zahnow 1995 (target_model), 478 keV from Bykov 2021, NACRE S-factors for ⁷Li(p,α) and ⁶Li, TUNL/Redigolo for ¹⁹F, Marta 2010 for the N resonances. PIXE is a binary-encounter scaling anchored on σ_K(Cu, 1 MeV) ≈ 70 b: ESTIMATE ×2–3. Interface fluorine: the beam leaves 20 µm Li at 872 keV at E_p = 1.10 MeV, which is the strongest ¹⁹F(p,αγ) resonance.

No contaminant can fake the signal; fluorine at the Li/stop interface can double the trigger rate at 1.10 MeV

6

Details

Boron is the only contaminant whose line lies inside the 13–18 MeV window (the ATOMKI ¹²C case), and it needs percent levels. The interface fluorine comes from the way the stop is cleaned before the Li goes on, or from perfluorinated pump oil in the evaporator; one short run at 1.10 MeV with a look at the 6.13 MeV line checks it.

Even the big plastics do not saturate: 478 keV makes 3 × 10⁵ hits/s per µA but none above the leg threshold

At 4 µA the big slab counts 1.2 × 10⁶ /s above 50 keV (≤ 311 keV Compton electrons): 12 % pile-up in 100 ns, +0.03 MeV on average; ~0.5 µA PMT anode current at 10 pe/MeV and gain 10⁶. The room (2 γ/cm²/s assumed) adds ~2 × 10³ /s.

Details

Geant4 γ-line libraries (26 lines, 2.6 × 10⁷ γ per detector and design) folded with the line spectrum. Ask the PMT/base of the big slabs once chosen: keep the divider current ≥ 20× the anode current.

478 keV fires SiPM bars but never the plastic: accidental legs 0.4 /s at 1 µA. Window, big plastics, P for ≥ 95 % live: 1.1 d at 0.25 µA, 0.28 d at 1 µA, 0.07 d at 4 µA to 3σ at ATOMKI.

8

Details

With P = 10 there are still ~9 cosmic MIPs per arm per second for the gain. Data at 1 µA, P = 10: ~100 Hz, 2.5 MB/s, 0.2 TB/day per FEU.

The window’s Mo K x-rays reach the Micromegas: 16 % occupancy per arm per µA; the dome keeps its Cu x-rays

A 17 keV point cluster per hit, bigger than a track’s ~8 keV in 30 mm. It triggers nothing, but it can steal the segment. Run ≤ 0.5 µA, add a 50 µm Cu foil on the MM windows (×0.1), cut point clusters.

9

Details

Diamond passes 96 % at 17.5 keV, mylar + 9 µm Cu ~60 %, the gas stops ~8 %. Ta instead of Mo is worse (L lines 8–10 keV from a larger σ_L). Measure with ¹⁰⁹Cd (22 keV) or a Mo-anode tube.

What could go wrong, ranked: the dome’s copper, the window’s x-rays, and fluorine at 1.10 MeV

Details

Not modelled: gate valve, tees, floor stand (no lepton reaches them); the grey parts are assumed PVC; PIXE is a scaling estimate; the room γ flux is a stand-in.

next

Build the 45° diamond window (200–300 µm, Ø20, Ti rings, Mo 8 µm) on a wide, short adapter, not the Cu dome; prescale the single-arm trigger; measure the Mo x-rays and the 6.13 MeV line early.

Ask Pierfrancesco: the grey flange material; how the Mo is deposited and cleaned (no fluorides); Li handling (Ar transfer). Next Geant4: the adapter shape, an Al/Be cup with a Mo liner, the Cu foil on the MM windows.
